sections.h2: What a Westfield seller faces between signing and closing
sections.html:
Westfield sellers deal with a fire department alarm check, a deed filed in Elizabeth and tax bills that arrive every quarter. The town asks for no resale certificate of occupancy. The unusual feature is price. The typical home sells just below the million-dollar line where a state surcharge starts, which makes the final price unusually important.

Below: the alarm inspection, deed filing, the state's transfer fee, tax billing, and how an agent, a solo sale and a cash buyer compare.

Westfield counted 32,595 residents in mid-2025, compared with 31,032 in 2020, and roughly 80 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. Buyers here often compare the town with Cranford, Scotch Plains and Mountainside, so the best pricing evidence is a handful of recent closings close to your own address.

Westfield station sits on NJ Transit's Raritan Valley Line. Off-peak trains run straight to New York Penn Station, and a few non-stop rush-hour trains head for Newark Penn. Bus 113 reaches the Port Authority terminal. By road, Route 28 follows the tracks, and Garden State Parkway Exits 135 and 137 and the Route 22 ramps are a short drive away.

Give buyers the walk time to the platform and the drive to the nearest ramp in your description. Commuters weigh those two numbers heavily, and they are easy to state.

sections.h2: Certificate of smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm compliance
sections.html:
Westfield's building department confirms that a home sale needs neither a certificate of occupancy nor a continued one. The one paper it does want is a Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance. Under state fire safety law, an owner of a one- or two-family house must obtain it from the Bureau of Fire Prevention before the buyer takes possession. Skipping it costs a $200 fine.

  • Crews inspect on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, and they do not phone ahead with an arrival time.
  • The fee depends on lead time: $100 for a slot more than ten business days out, $125 for four to ten, $150 for under four.
  • Someone aged 18 or over has to let the crew in, because they will not enter an empty house alone.
  • Sealed ten-year battery alarms pass, and so do hardwired detectors.
  • Close out any open construction permit before the visit.
  • Since March 14, 2025 the fire extinguisher is no longer part of the check.

The certificate arrives by email at the single address on the application, so use the one belonging to your closing attorney or agent. A house headed for demolition still needs one. With just two mornings a week on offer, request a date the moment you have a tentative closing day.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and the state transfer fee
sections.html:
Deeds for Westfield homes are filed with the Union County Clerk at the courthouse, 2 Broad Street, Elizabeth. The counter takes filings until 3:30 p.m. and wants no appointment. A second clerk's office in Westfield, on North Avenue East, handles passports, notary commissions and trade names, so deeds still go to Elizabeth. In practice your attorney or title company handles it.

The state's realty transfer fee is the seller's cost. On sales above $350,000 the first $150,000 is charged $2.90 per $500, the next slice up to $200,000 is $4.25, then $4.80 runs to $550,000, and $5.30 and $5.80 brackets follow. Westfield's typical $953,400 value falls in the $5.30 bracket.

Residential sales above $1,000,000 also owe the Graduated Percent Fee, which is 1 percent of the full price up to $2,000,000. An offer near that line is worth a quick calculation by your attorney first.

sections.h2: Property tax bills around a sale
sections.html:
Westfield's Tax Collector, at 425 E Broad Street, issues four bills a year due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. Each gets a grace period of ten calendar days, moving to the next business day when day ten is a weekend or holiday.

Late payments accrue 8 percent interest on the first $1,500 and 18 percent on the remainder, counted from the original due date. A returned check costs $20 more. Sewer fees run on a different cycle, due April 1.

A bill that never arrived is no excuse, so new owners should ask for one. Get a written payoff for tax and sewer before closing, and have the closing agent divide the current quarter. Senior and veteran relief applications also pass through this office, so confirm any deduction on the account is settled.

sections.h2: Agent, solo sale or cash buyer?
sections.html:
Listing with an agent usually exposes the house to the most buyers. A cash purchase is the quickest. Selling alone saves the commission but leaves every task to you. Condition and timing tend to settle it.

  • An agent fits a house that shows well, when you can live through open houses, buyer inspections and a lender's underwriting.
  • Going alone works if you already track sales on your block and will hire an attorney for the contract.
  • An as-is cash buyer suits an inherited house, a tenant who stays, or repairs you would rather skip before moving.

A cash sale avoids open houses and the lender's underwriting wait, though the alarm certificate and the filed deed still apply. Judge written offers by what remains after the transfer fee, any surcharge over $1,000,000, taxes and your loan payoff.

1. Hand the signed contract to your attorney.
  2. Book the Bureau of Fire Prevention for a Tuesday or Thursday morning.
  3. Close open permits and line up an adult to be home.
  4. Ask the Tax Collector for the tax and sewer payoff in writing.
  5. If you owe a mortgage, order a payoff letter from the lender.
  6. On closing day the deed goes to the clerk in Elizabeth.

The alarm certificate is the likeliest cause of delay, since inspection slots are scarce.

faqs.q: What costs come with selling a Westfield house?
faqs.a: The seller pays the state realty transfer fee, which follows the price, plus a fire department inspection of $100 to $150. Sales above $1,000,000 add a 1 percent surcharge. A listing agent's commission, if you use one, is separate.

faqs.q: Is an inspection needed before closing in Westfield?
faqs.a: Yes, an alarm and carbon monoxide inspection by the Bureau of Fire Prevention. No certificate of occupancy is needed. Crews come on Tuesday and Thursday mornings.

faqs.q: What are the Westfield tax installments?
faqs.a: Four bills fall due on the first of February, May, August and November, each with a ten-day cushion. Sewer is separate and due April 1. Late interest is 8 percent up to $1,500 and 18 percent beyond.

faqs.q: Can a Westfield house with problems still sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The alarm check covers only alarms and detectors, though open permits must be closed. A buyer can take on cosmetic or structural work, which is how as-is purchases function.

faqs.q: Which office files a Westfield deed?
faqs.a: The Union County Clerk in Elizabeth, at 2 Broad Street. Walk-in filing needs no appointment, and your closing attorney or title company normally files it for you.
